rounds.text: CMX Holdings Ltd presents a compelling turnaround profile supported by a strong sector tailwind in Financial Services, which currently holds a tailwind score of +0.78 [E37, E39]. Crucially, results are actively improving with a results score of 73 out of 100, featuring net profit up 14% year-over-year, sequential profit growth, and accelerating earnings growth [E34, E35, E36, E38]. This operational momentum is underscored by a solid Return on Equity of 12.4%, outperforming the sector benchmark of 5.58% [E8]. Furthermore, foreign institutions have increased their stake by 2.34 percentage points since December 2023, signaling early smart-money accumulation [E26]. Long-term compounding also demonstrates underlying resilience, with 3-year and 5-year share price growth reaching 32% and 15% respectively [E15, E16]. conceded: [E12], [E21], [E22], [E25].

CMX Holdings Ltd carries severe fundamental risks, highlighted most prominently by a catastrophic top-line collapse featuring a compounded sales growth rate of -100% over the trailing twelve months [E12]. This operational failure directly feeds into deeply negative return metrics, including a ROCE of -50.8% [E11] and an unsupportable P/E ratio of -45.74x compared to the sector benchmark of 17.93x [E5]. Furthermore, the company burns cash, evidenced by a negative operating cash flow and free cash flow of Rs -1.64 Cr in Mar 2026 [E21, E22], while simultaneously sitting on rising borrowings of Rs 7.98 Cr as of Sep 2026 [E23]. Compounding these operational distress signals, insiders are actively exiting, with promoter holding dropping by 12.53 percentage points from 64.30% in Dec 2023 to 51.77% in Sep 2026 [E25]. Conceded: [E8].

While the bear highlights a compounded sales growth figure of -100% [E12], this contrasts directly with documented fundamental acceleration, including a net profit increase of 14% year-on-year, quarter-on-quarter profit gains, and accelerating earnings growth [E34, E35, E36]. The criticism regarding negative returns via ROCE [E11] overlooks an annualized Return on Equity of 12.4%, which outpaces the sector benchmark of 5.58% [E8]. Conceded: [E21, E22, E23]. Although borrowings and insider reductions are flagged [E23, E25], foreign institutional investors have simultaneously increased their stake to 2.34% from zero [E26]. Finally, the negative sentiment and cautious price-to-earnings ratios [E5] ignore the company's operational turnaround, which scores 73 out of 100 on results while operating inside a financial services sector experiencing a robust macro tailwind score of +0.78 [E37, E38, E39].

Conceded: [E34, E35, E36]. The claimed fundamental acceleration and profit gains completely ignore the catastrophic top-line collapse shown by compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months dropping to -100% [E12]. While the bull points to an ROE of 12.4% [E8], this metric stands in stark contrast to severe capital destruction evidenced by a negative ROCE of -50.8% [E11] and a negative ROCE of -29.57% against the sector benchmark [E9]. Furthermore, dismissing insider selling [E25, E32] by pointing to a minor 2.34% foreign institutional stake [E26] fails to justify why promoters have dumped 12.53 percentage points of their holdings since December 2023 [E25]. Finally, relying on sector tailwinds and operational turnaround scores [E37, E38, E39] cannot excuse a business suffering from negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -1.64 Cr [E21, E22], rising borrowings [E23], and a low interest coverage ratio flag [E31].
